inverse: The module declaration unit itself cannot parse a case, write a protocol or select a verdict; such traces require a caller into another module. This is a syntactic exclusion, not whole-library nonbehavior.

From the exported module-name set, compatible source antecedents include arbitrary module bodies and documentation with the same public declarations. Export names do not reconstruct signatures or implementation.
Each of seven pub mod declarations admits external name lookup; changing one to private breaks callers using that path. Integration tests are actual compile evidence for used paths only.
Rust resolves modules at compile time relative to src/lib.rs. No runtime module discovery occurs, and declaration order is not execution order.

Integration callers use rule::Rule with juris::Jurisdiction and court::Case, then report/absurd/measure/extract functions. Shared type identity comes from one crate compilation, not string matching module labels.
